This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed
investing to full-service wealth management all in one place. No matter
your investing goal, life stage, amount to invest or know-how, you can invest your
way with Schwab. This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour. Live from
NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston. At least 12 people are dead
after a missile attack on the airport in Riyadh. Officials in Saudi Arabia say
more than 300 others were wounded. The Saudi-led coalition blames Yemen's Iran
backed Houthi rebels and is vowed to respond. President Trump is defending his
new agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin that would bring more
Russian diesel fuel to the global market. Following a campaign stop in Tennessee
last night, Trump said Putin wants to end the war in Ukraine. He'd like to see a
settlement. President Putin would like to see a settlement strongly. And look, he's
he's freeing up a lot of oil for the world, okay? That's a good thing. And by the
way, at a very low price. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky
calls the deal not fair and not honest. He says money from Russian fuel sales
will help finance the war. Republican candidates immersed in scandal are
playing an outsized role in this year's midterm elections. NPR's Claudia
Grisalis reports several congressional races are in play because of the
controversies. Cook Political Report has shifted races tied to the embattled
candidates in North Carolina, Ohio and Texas from leaning Republican to toss-ups.
Elaine Kamark, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, says that could
be part of a one-to-punch for Republicans facing political headwinds. If you're a
Republican, you're facing a wave here, a blue wave, then you really, really,
really don't need a scandal. North Carolina's Chuck Edwards left his race
over sexual harassment claims, leaving his replacement in a competitive fight.
Ohio's Max Miller saw a race setback after domestic violence allegations and a
Cook political analyst says scandal plagued Ken Paxton's run for Senate is
dragging down the entire ticket in Texas. Claudia Grisalis, NPR News. An investigation
is underway into a mass shooting that left nine people dead in northwestern
Pennsylvania on Friday. NPR's Chantaliz Duster reports police in Erie say
children were among the fatalities. Erie police say a woman who was eight months
pregnant and a 10-month-old baby were among those killed in the shooting that
took place at a home. The suspected gunman also died from a
self-inflicted gunshot wound, according to police. Police responded to an alert
of gunshots at the home and when they arrived they found two women dead
outside. Investigators believe the deaths occurred before law enforcement arrived.
Eight people were family members and one was a family friend, according to police.
Erie police say they are investigating a possible motive. They also said the
suspected shooter had a history with law enforcement but did not give details.
Chantaliz Duster, NPR News. This is NPR News in Washington. Death row inmate
Christa Pike has been discharged from the hospital and is recovering in a
prison rehabilitation center. The 50-year-old survived an execution
attempt by lethal injection. Her attorneys are calling on the governor of
Tennessee to change her sentence from death to life without parole. Pike has
spent the last 30 years in prison for the 1995 murder of her 19-year-old
classmate Colleen Slemmer. Police in India have freed the leaders of a
movement that's calling for protests surrounding the controversial revision
of voter rolls, even as they call for more demonstrations. NPR's Deahadeed
reports it's the latest political crisis to royal the government of Prime
Minister Narendra Modi. The release of the three men came a day after they were
removed from their airline seats and detained by police just as their flight
touched down in the capital. They were among the thousands detained on
Saturday as security forces tried to stave off protests. The forces barricaded
parts of downtown Delhi, cut off the internet in parts of the city, shut down
metro stations and railway lines and ban gatherings. Still, protests play. Demonstrators
are demanding the resignation of the election commissioner after a revision of
voter rolls struck off more than 130 million people or forced them to justify
why they should be allowed to stay on the rolls. The Prime Minister has not
addressed the controversy. Deahadeed, NPR News, New Delhi. I'm Windsor Johnston, NPR
News in Washington. This message comes from Charles Schwab with their original
podcast Choiceology hosted by Katie Milkman, an award-winning behavioral
scientist and author of the best-selling book How to Change. Choiceology is a show
about the psychology and economics behind people's decisions. Hear true
stories from Nobel laureates, historians, authors, athletes and more about how to
make better decisions to help avoid costly mistakes. Download the latest
episode and subscribe at Schwab.com/podcast or wherever you listen.

topics.text: Missile attack on Riyadh airport kills at least 12 and wounds over 300, Saudi officials say
Trump defends new Russian diesel fuel deal with Putin, as Zelensky calls it unfair and dishonest
Scandal-plagued Republican candidates in NC, Ohio and Texas shift Cook ratings toward toss-ups
Erie, Pennsylvania police investigate home shooting that killed nine, including children and a pregnant woman
Death row inmate Christa Pike discharged from hospital after failed lethal injection; attorneys seek life sentence
Indian police free protest leaders as nationwide demonstrations continue over voter roll revision in Delhi
